instructions: You are Northwind's travel assistant. Answer employees' questions about travel and expenses using the policy below. Be concise and accurate.
context:
## 1. Purpose and scope

Northwind Analytics ("the company") expects employees to travel when travel is the most effective way to serve clients, build relationships with colleagues, and grow professionally. This policy explains what the company pays for, how trips are approved, and how expenses are reported. It aims to balance employee comfort and safety with responsible use of company funds.

This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees, interns, and contractors whose contracts reference it. Where local law or a works council agreement sets different rules, those rules take precedence for employees in that jurisdiction. Questions not covered here should be directed to Finance Operations through the #ask-finance channel.

All amounts in this policy are in US dollars (USD). Expenses incurred in other currencies are converted at the card network rate on the transaction date, or, for cash expenses, at the rate shown in TripDesk on the date of the expense.

### 3.1 Approval

Every trip needs approval in TripDesk before anything is booked.

- Domestic trips with an estimated total cost of 3,000 USD or less need your manager's approval.
- Domestic trips over 3,000 USD, and all international trips regardless of cost, need approval from both your manager and your director.

The estimated total cost includes flights, lodging, meals per diem, ground transportation, and any registration fees.

### 3.2 Booking

Book flights, hotels, and rental cars through TripDesk so the company can support you if plans change and so bookings are covered by our travel insurance. Bookings made outside TripDesk are reimbursed only if they cost less than the lowest comparable TripDesk option on the day of booking; attach a screenshot as proof.

Book flights at least 14 days before departure whenever possible. Bookings made fewer than 7 days before departure require a short explanation in TripDesk.

### 3.3 Travel insurance and safety

The company's travel insurance covers medical emergencies, evacuation, trip interruption, and lost luggage for all business trips booked through TripDesk. Do not buy additional travel insurance; it is not reimbursed.

International travelers must register their itinerary with SafeRoute, our travel safety provider, at least 3 days before departure. SafeRoute sends security alerts and can arrange assistance 24/7.

### 4.1 Class of service

Class of service depends on the scheduled flight time of the longest single segment of the trip:

- Under 6 hours: economy class.
- 6 to 10 hours: premium economy is allowed.
- Over 10 hours: business class is allowed with your manager's approval, obtained in advance in TripDesk.

First class is never reimbursed. You may upgrade at your own expense or with personal loyalty points.

### 4.2 Fares and extras

Choose the lowest logical fare: the cheapest fare with reasonable departure times (between 7:00 and 21:00 local time) and no more than one additional connection compared to the fastest option. Refundable fares are allowed only when the trip dates are likely to change.

Reimbursable extras:

- One checked bag per trip, each way.
- Seat selection up to 40 USD per flight.
- In-flight Wi-Fi up to 30 USD per trip, when you need to work during the flight.

Airport lounge memberships, priority boarding, and extra legroom seats above the 40 USD seat allowance are not reimbursed.

### 4.3 Rail instead of air

For journeys where the train takes under 4 hours door to door, take the train instead of flying. Standard class is the default; first class is allowed on trains when the fare difference is under 25 USD.

### 5.1 Nightly caps

Hotel caps apply per night and include taxes and mandatory fees. Caps depend on the city tier:

- **Tier 1 — 320 USD per night:** New York City, San Francisco, Boston, London, Zurich, Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney.
- **Tier 2 — 230 USD per night:** Chicago, Seattle, Los Angeles, Washington DC, Toronto, Berlin, Paris, Amsterdam, Madrid, Dublin.
- **Tier 3 — 160 USD per night:** all other locations.

### 5.2 Exceptions

When attending a conference, you may book the official conference hotel through the conference room block at up to 15% above the nightly cap. Note the conference name in TripDesk.

Short-term rentals (for example apartments) are allowed when they cost less than the nightly cap for that city and are booked through TripDesk.

If you stay with friends or family instead of a hotel, you may expense a thank-you gift of up to 50 USD per trip.

### 5.3 Not reimbursed at hotels

Minibar, in-room movies, spa and gym fees, room upgrades, and late checkout fees (unless caused by a delayed flight) are not reimbursed. Laundry is reimbursed only for trips of 6 nights or more, up to 30 USD per week.

## 7. Ground transportation

- **Taxis and rideshare** are reimbursed with receipts. Choose standard options, not premium or luxury classes.
- **Public transport** is encouraged and reimbursed with receipts or a card statement.
- **Rental cars** must be compact class unless you are traveling with three or more colleagues. Rent a car only when it is cheaper than taxis or public transport for the trip. Refuel before returning the car; refueling charges from the rental company are not reimbursed.
- **Personal car:** you may claim 0.64 USD per mile instead of fuel costs. Claim the actual round-trip distance. Tolls and parking are reimbursed with receipts. Traffic and parking fines are never reimbursed.

### 9.1 Deadlines

Submit your expense report in TripDesk within 30 days after the trip ends.

- Reports submitted 31 to 60 days after the trip ends need your manager's sign-off with a short reason for the delay.
- Expenses submitted more than 60 days after the trip ends are not reimbursed.

### 9.2 Receipts

Attach an itemized receipt for every single expense of 25 USD or more. Per diem meals don't need receipts. If a receipt is lost, submit a missing receipt declaration in TripDesk; more than two declarations in a calendar year are reviewed by Finance Operations.
